lesson.title: The -ai Future
lesson.subtitle: Infinitive + avoir's present endings: je parlerai, tu visiteras, on ira.

hook.title: The -ai Future: Why Every Future Stem Ends in /ʁ/
hook.content: To form the one-word future tense (le futur simple), take the whole infinitive (parler, visiter, finir) or a core /ʁ/ stem (être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, faire → fer-, venir → viendr-, voir → verr-) and attach the present endings of avoir (-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont)!

footnotes.title: One Stem Serves BOTH the Future (-ai) and the Conditional (-ais)!
footnotes.content: Every irregular future stem (ser-, aur-, ir-, fer-, viendr-, verr-) is ALSO the exact stem of the Conditional Would-World! Put -ai/-a on it for 'will' (ce sera 'it will be'); put -ais/-ait on it for 'would' (ce serait 'it would be')!

pattern.title: Future Stem (Ending in -r-) + avoir Endings (-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont)
pattern.content: Spot the /ʁ/ stem and read -ai/-as/-a as 'will' and -ais/-ait as 'would'!
pattern.linguist_note: Synthetic Romance future (< infinitive + habēre) and conditional (< infinitive + habēbam) share 100% of their stems.
pattern.trap_note: Don't confuse je parlerai (-ai = 'I will speak') with je parlerais (-ais = 'I would speak') on the page!

exercises.prompt: Match each future form with its English meaning and stem:

matching_pairs.german: I will speak / I will visit

exercises.target_answer: I will speak / I will visit, it will be (que sera, sera!), I will go, you will see, I will come
exercises.meaning: je parlerai / je visiterai (infinitive + ai), ce sera (ser- from être), j'irai (ir- from aller), tu verras (verr- from voir), je viendrai (viendr- from venir)
exercises.explanation: Every future stem in the entire French language ends in the letter R!

exercises.prompt: The French future of être ('ce _____' = 'it will be') appears in the famous song refrain 'Whatever will be, will be'. Type that four-letter verb form:
exercises.meaning: Que sera, sera ↔ ce sera ('it will be')
exercises.explanation: ser- is the future/conditional stem of être: ce sera ('it will be'), ce serait ('it would be').

exercises.prompt: Compare 'I will do it' (future) vs. 'I would do it' (conditional) using the stem 'fer-' of faire:
options: Je le ferais / Je le ferai
Je le faireai / Je le faireais
Je le ferai / Je le ferais
exercises.target_answer: Je le ferai / Je le ferais
exercises.explanation: The stem fer- is identical for both; -ai is future and -ais is conditional.

exercises.idea: you will see tomorrow it will be very good
cues: You will see tomorrow → Tu verras demain
it will be very good → ce sera très bon
idea_parts: second future → ce sera très bon
exercises.target_answer: Tu verras demain, ce sera très bon
exercises.meaning: You will see tomorrow, it will be very good
exercises.explanation: Tu verras (from voir) and ce sera (from être) are top-frequency future phrases.

diagnosis.cue: Use ce sera ('it will be') for the future of c'est.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Je vous appellerai quand j'arriverai à Paris
exercises.target_answer: Je vous appellerai quand j'arriverai à Paris
exercises.meaning: I will call you when I arrive in Paris
exercises.explanation: After quand ('when') referring to the future, French uses the future tense (quand j'arriverai)!
exercises.affirmation: You wrote both -ai future forms cleanly!

summary.outcome: Recognize and form the -ai future tense on regular verbs and core stems (sera, aura, ira, fera, viendra, verra).

use_example.german: Tu verras, ce sera une belle aventure !
use_example.english: You'll see, it will be a great adventure!

summary.takeaway: Every future stem ends in -r-; add -ai/-as/-a for 'will' and -ais/-ait for 'would'.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([27] il faut): see how The -ai Future leads directly into il faut.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "You will see tomorrow, it will be very good" in French:
twist.target_answer: Tu verras demain, ce sera très bon
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Tu verras demain, ce sera très bon" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of The -ai Future.

aller.context_translation: I'm going to go to the café.
aller.etymology_derivation: Latin ambulāre 'to walk' → ambler → aller. To go is a stroll away — and the near future rides on it.

avoir.etymology_derivation: Latin habēre = have. The H dropped and stayed dropped — French never pronounces its Latin H.

être.etymology_derivation: Latin esse 'to be' → essere → être. English kept the root in essence and quintessential — the being-ness inside the word.

faire.context_translation: What are you going to do?
faire.etymology_derivation: One French verb covers both 'do' and 'make' (like Spanish hacer and German machen).

voir.context_translation: I'm going to see my friend.
voir.etymology_derivation: Latin vidēre lost its middle d: vedere → veoir → voir.

venir.etymology_derivation: Prefix it to build a whole family: revenir (come back), devenir (become), prévenir (warn).

visiter.etymology_derivation: visitation → visiter. The rare English noun unlocks the everyday verb: don't decide too quickly that you can't say it.

demain.context_translation: Tomorrow, I'm going to visit Lyon.
